analysis.title: These Are The States Where Tuesday's Midterms Can Pull The Plug On Data Centers
key_insights: BofA's utilities team (Ross Fowler) finds data center pause or moratorium proposals in 20 of the 36 governor races on the ballot, including Texas. BofA frames the cycle as a story about regulators and data center rules, not party control.

BofA sorts the 36 races into four buckets: five states that matter most (TX, GA, OH, PA, OR), six where the market is probably overpricing election risk (AZ, FL, IA, KS, MI, WI), a group with solid constructs and little election risk (led by WY, MN, CO, ID), and three where an upset would be a genuine surprise (AL, AR, OK).

Stock consequences run through three channels per BofA: who the winner appoints to the utility commission and when, whether the large load framework is already written, and how far campaign positions can travel against a Legislature, statute or elected commission.

Data center bills went from a rounding error in 2024 to roughly 80 enacted or under consideration this year, and local moratoriums, zoning restrictions and ordinances rose to well over 250 (datacentertracker.org via BofA economists). Wells Fargo flagged a fourfold jump in active local moratoriums in September.

BofA economists see state and local governments, which control zoning, land use and permitting, as the more immediate constraint. They expect those measures to slow construction at the margin and raise costs, not derail the broader data-center investment cycle.

AdImpact (via Time): $137.6 million spent on broadcast ads about data centers this cycle, 77% by Democrats. Only 7% of voters rank data centers as a top issue, so the ads mainly target electric bills.

BofA expects capital to 'sort rather than stop' after the election, flowing toward Wyoming, Minnesota, Iowa, Wisconsin, Kansas, Nevada, South Carolina and Tennessee. Existing projects should be grandfathered outside the TCEQ review in Texas.

Texas is 'the single most consequential election for utilities and power this cycle'. The next governor inherits a 474 GW interconnection queue, about 90% data centers and more than five times the all-time system peak.

Texas Gov. Abbott directed an audit of data centers in interconnection on Aug 3, ERCOT paused Batch Zero and halted energization approvals for data center and crypto loads of 75 MW or more, and on Sept 21 Abbott ordered TCEQ to halt all data center permits, including islanded facilities with behind-the-meter generation.

Texas race: a YouGov poll (Sept 28 to Oct 5) had Hinojosa 48% vs Abbott 47%. BofA sees little evidence equities price any chance of a change in governor. BofA says the Texas backdrop is decided in 1H27, not on November 3.

ERCOT conditionally classified 204 projects (66.4 GW) as base load and 158 projects (127.9 GW) as studied load on Sept 3, with a verification audit due Dec 10. Bloomberg estimates close to 50 GW, about 20% of the national pipeline, is at risk from the Texas pause, with up to $8 billion in revenue implications by Q1 2027.

Texas legislature: prefiling for the 90th session opens Nov 9 and BofA expects at least 60 data center bills. The sales tax exemption, costing about $3.3 billion, is in the crosshairs. The PUCT approved Import Paths 1 and 3 of the $33 billion Permian Basin Reliability Plan and remanded Path 2.

BofA says the range of outcomes for Texas utilities (SRE via Oncor, CNP, AEP, VST) is wider than the stocks imply and recommends carrying materially wider volatility margins. Banks are reportedly stuck with a $15 billion bridge loan for Anthropic's Texas campus after the freeze killed the bond takeout.

Georgia: Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms backs a temporary statewide pause, Republican Rick Jackson opposes a moratorium. Two of five PSC seats are on the ballot with Republicans holding 3-2, so Democrats need both to take control and could institute Hubbard's data center cost framework regardless of the governor result. BofA flags this as the key risk for Southern Co. (SO), whose Georgia Power has a base rate freeze through 2028.
15 seats across nine elected commissions are contested, with party control in play in Georgia, Louisiana (ETR buildout) and North Dakota.

Ohio: both Acton (D) and Ramaswamy (R) propose a conditional moratorium. Ohio has 21 of the 35 local data center measures on ballots, 16 of 35 would ban or cap facilities, and about 12 point the other way. BofA would not underwrite a significant growth trajectory for AEP and FirstEnergy until the policy framework settles.
Pennsylvania PUC review of ROEs, DSIC and large-load ratemaking matters more than the ballot for PPL, EXC and FE. Oregon's wildfire policy is the defining valuation issue for POR and AVA.

BofA has Buy ratings on CMS and DTE (Michigan), EVRG (Kansas), LNT (Iowa, Wisconsin) and PNW (Arizona), where it thinks election risk is overpriced. Michigan moratorium expected to be brief, Kansas faces a Republican supermajority.
Best-framework states per BofA: Black Hills (BKH) in Wyoming (9.75% ROE, 52% equity ratio, ~3.1 GW online by 2031), Xcel (XEL) in Minnesota and Colorado, and IDACORP (IDA) in Idaho.

Alabama HB 475 expands the PSC to seven and creates a governor-appointed Secretary of Energy. Doug Jones wants a one-year moratorium and Tuberville a four-year rate freeze, so even the base case carries risk for SO. Arkansas (ETR) and Oklahoma (OGE, AEP) are the unlikely upsets.

Federal: Piper Sandler puts 55% odds on a Democratic sweep and 50/50 on the BAAJA permitting bill passing in the lame duck, which would push data centers to cover their energy costs and use behind-the-meter power. Goldman sees behind-the-meter generation powering 25% of data centers by 2030. BofA economists expect limited federal restraint on AI over two years.

Key dates: Nov 9 (Texas prefiling), Dec 10 (ERCOT Batch Zero audit), Q1/Q2 2027 (final allocations). The author agrees the market is not worried enough about Texas but doubts the pause is only temporary, and expects the audit to shrink the 474 GW queue.

tension_points.bull_case: BofA notes consensus holds that Abbott reverts to a pro data center stance after a win, and Texas remains the clearest secular demand growth story in the sector.
tension_points.bear_case: The audit, CCN remands and legislative docket carry institutional momentum independent of the governor, and equities price no chance of a governor change. The author expects the audit to shrink the 474 GW queue.
tension_points.what_invalidates: ERCOT's Dec 10 verification audit and final Batch Zero allocations in 1H27, plus the 90th Legislature's treatment of the sales tax exemption after prefiling opens Nov 9.

tension_points.bull_case: BofA sees most pause talk as sequencing rather than opposition, with capital sorting rather than stopping and existing projects grandfathered.
tension_points.bear_case: The author argues that a Republican in Texas and Ohio and a Democrat in Georgia all landing on a pause makes pause look like the new default.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Post-election enacted moratoriums that cover existing projects, or the Texas TCEQ review extending beyond 1H27.
